claims.text: Closed-loop, real-time laser power modulation during laser powder-bed fusion will reduce thermal fluctuations in high-entropy-alloy components.
Reducing thermal fluctuations will minimize fabrication-induced defects and residual stresses.
Minimizing defects and residual stresses will improve dimensional precision and mechanical integrity.
The current fabrication baseline uses fixed laser power during powder-bed fusion of high-entropy-alloy powders.
Real-time power modulation based on in-situ melt-pool imaging will produce more uniform melt-pool dynamics.
More uniform melt-pool dynamics will minimize localized overheating and underheating.
Minimizing localized overheating and underheating will reduce porosity and residual-stress hotspots and provide finer microstructural control.
Melt-pool imaging feedback allows dynamic laser-power adjustments that maintain an optimal melt-pool size and temperature.
Maintaining an optimal melt-pool size and temperature prevents excessive thermal gradients and rapid-solidification defects.
Preventing excessive thermal gradients and rapid-solidification defects reduces distortion and internal defects while improving mechanical integrity.
Relative to fixed-power processing, closed-loop modulation will improve dimensional accuracy, including reduced distortion and better adherence to design geometry.
Relative to fixed-power processing, closed-loop modulation will increase tensile strength and ductility.
Relative to fixed-power processing, closed-loop modulation will reduce porosity.
The predicted benefits are expected to hold for high-entropy alloys processed by laser powder-bed fusion under an inert atmosphere with integrated in-situ monitoring.
Changes in environmental conditions or substantially different alloy systems may alter the effectiveness of the intervention.
